headline: Australian house prices forecast to fall 5-10% peak to trough as tax changes on capital gains and negative gearing freeze investor activity
reasoning: Landahl explains that changes to capital gains tax and negative gearing have effectively stopped investors in their tracks, though investors with existing property are not selling, reducing liquidity. Investors still active are pivoting toward higher-yielding properties given the changed after-tax return profile. Sydney and Melbourne are recording negative growth, while Perth and Brisbane are also falling, with most market forecasters pencilling in a 5-10% annualised peak-to-trough decline. He warns of significant unintended consequences including rising rents, low vacancy rates, and a looming supply crisis for renters as new investor-funded stock fails to come to market.
quote: Perth Brisbane and our falling Sydney and Melbourne are recording are negative growth at the moment. So most are forecasting 5 to 10% annualized from peak to trough. Ah fall in growth. Is that bringing home buyers back in the market? I think it's creating opportunities for home buyers because the market has slowed. But I think there's a lot of unintended consequences around it's investors are holding stock are there's not new investment stock coming. So there's a massive issue looming for renters. We're already seeing low vacancy rates. We're already seeing rents rising. Investors in the market are looking for higher yielding properties now because their strategy has changed. So I don't think the full consequence of the tax changes have played out yet. But the market has. The market is falling, and I think we're going to see a few more months of pretty slow activity in the market.
